Is one of the parties the State, a wilaya, a commune or a public establishment of administrative character? The organic criterion of CPCA art. 800 sends the case to the administrative court, whatever the nature of the dispute.

Which actions belong to the administrative court by their object (annulment, interpretation and review of legality of administrative decisions; full-jurisdiction claims; matters given by special texts) under CPCA art. 801?

Which exceptions bring a case with a public body back to the ordinary courts (CPCA art. 802: road offences; liability claims for damage caused by any vehicle belonging to the State, a wilaya, a commune or a public administrative establishment)?

Is the public party an establishment of industrial and commercial character (EPIC) or a public economic enterprise? These are not listed in art. 800 and are normally sued before the ordinary courts; check the special text.
Is the incompetence of the administrative or ordinary court ratione materiae of public order, can it be raised at any stage, and must the judge raise it of his own motion (CPCA art. 36 and art. 807)?

What happens when the ordinary court finds it has no jurisdiction because the matter is administrative: declaration of incompetence, no transfer; the lawyer must refile before the competent administrative court.

Time limit for an action for annulment before the administrative court: four months from notification of the individual decision or publication of the regulatory decision (CPCA art. 829); optional administrative grievance and its effect (art. 830); forfeiture.

Territorial jurisdiction of the administrative courts (CPCA arts. 803 and 804) and the administrative courts of appeal created in 2022; the Council of State as first and last instance for central authorities (art. 901 as amended).

Is the claimant a civil servant or an agent under the general statute of public service? Individual labour disputes of such agents fall outside Law 90-11 and go to the administrative court, not the social section.
Conflicts of jurisdiction between the two orders: Tribunal des conflits (Organic Law 98-03); the referral mechanism when both orders declare themselves incompetent.

Specialised commercial courts (CPCA art. 536 bis and following, added by Law 22-13 of 2022): the list of matters (intellectual property; commercial companies, their dissolution and liquidation; bankruptcy and judicial settlement; banks and financial institutions with merchants; maritime and air transport and insurance; international trade).
Is the specialised commercial court competence exclusive and of public order, and what happens to a case filed in the commercial section of an ordinary court that belongs to it?

Mandatory conciliation before filing in the specialised commercial court (CPCA art. 536 bis 4 or nearby): who conducts it, its time limit, the record, the sanction of failing to attempt it (inadmissibility?).
Composition of the specialised commercial court (a judge with assessors) and the seats and territorial competence fixed by executive decree.
Is the employer bankrupt or in judicial settlement? Then claims against the estate may need to be declared to the trustee and the bankruptcy court; check Commercial Code arts. 244 and following.
The criminal judge: the civil action for damages arising from an offence may be brought with the public action before the criminal court (CPP arts. 2 and 3) or separately before the civil judge.

When the civil action is brought before the civil judge while the public action is pending, the civil judge must stay until the criminal judgment (CPP art. 4: the criminal holds the civil in abeyance).

Irrevocable choice of route (CPP art. 5): a party who brought the civil action before the civil court cannot bring it before the criminal court, unless the prosecution was started before the civil court ruled on the merits.
Authority of the criminal judgment over the civil judge on facts necessarily established (Civil Code art. 339 or similar); a prior criminal conviction as proof of the fault.
Limitation of the civil action joined to a public action follows the civil limitation rules (CPP art. 10); check the module periods.
Order to pay (أمر بالأداء, CPCA arts. 306 and following): a sum of money, fixed, liquid and due, established by a written instrument (acknowledgement of debt, commercial paper).
Prior step for the order to pay: a demand for payment (تكليف بالوفاء) served by a bailiff, with a period (perhaps 15 days) before the petition can be filed.

Procedure of the order to pay: petition in two copies to the president of the court with the written evidence; decision within a short period (perhaps five days); no appeal against refusal; the creditor then follows the ordinary procedure.

Opposition to the order to pay: the debtor may oppose within a period (perhaps fifteen days) from service; the order becomes enforceable failing opposition; the order lapses if not served within a set period.
Is the order to pay optional (the creditor may still file an ordinary claim) or compulsory where its conditions are met? I believe it is optional.
Orders on petition (أوامر على العرائض) and summary proceedings (الاستعجال): procedures inside the ordinary court that replace or precede a claim; they are not exits but must be distinguished.
Arbitration clause or compromise: the ordinary court must not hear a case submitted to arbitration if a party raises it; it is not of public order (CPCA arts. 1006 and following).
Tax disputes, customs and social security disputes: special commissions or prior administrative recourse before any court; check the special laws.
Expropriation for public utility and administrative contracts (public procurement): administrative court, even if the claim is for money.

Cases that look like exits and are not: a claim against a public economic enterprise; a claim for damage by a public vehicle; a claim by a worker of a private employer; a commercial claim not in the list of the specialised court (commercial section of the ordinary court).
Defendant residing abroad: the Algerian courts still have jurisdiction (CPCA arts. 41 and 42 for Algerian parties); this is international jurisdiction, not an exit to another order.
Amendments to remember: Law 22-13 of 12 July 2022 (specialised commercial courts, administrative courts of appeal); Law 08-09 of 25 February 2008 (CPCA); Organic Law 22-10 on judicial organisation.
